0: Khlestakov and Marya Antonovna. MARYA. Oh!
1: KHLESTAKOV. What frightened you so, mademoiselle?
3: KHLESTAKOV [showing off]. Please, miss. It's a great pleasure to me that you took me for a man who—May I venture to ask you where you were going?
4: MARYA. I really wasn't going anywhere.
5: KHLESTAKOV. But why weren't you going anywhere?
6: MARYA. I was wondering whether mamma was here.
7: KHLESTAKOV. No. I'd like to know why you weren't going anywhere.
8: MARYA. I should have been in your way. You were occupied with important matters.
9: KHLESTAKOV [showing off]. Your eyes are better than important matters. You cannot possibly disturb me. No, indeed, by no means. On the contrary, you afford me great pleasure.
10: MARYA. You speak like a man from the capital.
11: KHLESTAKOV. For such a beautiful lady as you. May I give myself the pleasure of offering you a chair? But no, you should have, not a chair, but a throne.
12: MARYA. I really don't know—I really must go [She sits down.]
13: KHLESTAKOV. What a beautiful scarf that is.
14: MARYA. You are making fun of me. You're only ridiculing the provincials.
15: KHLESTAKOV. Oh, mademoiselle, how I long to be your scarf, so that I might embrace your lily neck.
16: MARYA. I haven't the least idea what you are talking about—scarf!—Peculiar weather today, isn't it?
17: KHLESTAKOV. Your lips, mademoiselle, are better than any weather.
18: MARYA. You are just saying that—I should like to ask you—I'd rather you would write some verses in my album for a souvenir. You must know very many.
19: KHLESTAKOV. Anything you desire, mademoiselle. Ask! What verses will you have?
20: MARYA. Any at all. Pretty, new verses.
21: KHLESTAKOV. Oh, what are verses! I know a lot of them.
22: MARYA. Well, tell me. What verses will you write for me?
23: KHLESTAKOV. What's the use? I know them anyway.
25: KHLESTAKOV. I have lots of them—of every sort. If you like, for example, I'll give you this: "Oh, thou, mortal man, who in thy anguish murmurest against God—" and others. I can't remember them now. Besides, it's all bosh. I'd rather offer you my love instead, which ever since your first glance—[Moves his chair nearer.]
26: MARYA. Love? I don't understand love. I never knew what love is. [Moves her chair away.]
27: KHLESTAKOV. Why do you move your chair away? It is better for us to sit near each other.
28: MARYA [moving away]. Why near? It's all the same if it's far away.
29: KHLESTAKOV [moving nearer]. Why far? It's all the same if it's near.
31: KHLESTAKOV [moving nearer]. It only seems near to you. Imagine it's far. How happy I would be, mademoiselle, if I could clasp you in my embrace.
32: MARYA [looking through the window]. What is that? It looked as if something had flown by. Was it a magpie or some other bird?
33: KHLESTAKOV [kisses her shoulder and looks through the window]. It's a magpie.
34: MARYA [rises indignantly]. No, that's too much—Such rudeness, such impertinence.
35: KHLESTAKOV [holding her back]. Forgive me, mademoiselle. I did it only out of love—only out of love, nothing else.
36: MARYA. You take me for a silly provincial wench. [Struggles to go away.]
37: KHLESTAKOV [still holding her back]. It's out of love, really—out of love. It was just a little fun. Marya Antonovna, don't be angry. I'm ready to beg your forgiveness on my knees. [Falls on his knees.] Forgive me, do forgive me! You see, I am on my knees.
